title: U.S. House · Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District
area: East-central Wisconsin, including Sheboygan, Fond du Lac, and Oshkosh.

context.text: Incumbent Glenn Grothman (R) advanced from the Republican primary with 99.7% of the vote. Bradley Smith defeated Amanda Bell 50.3%-49.7% in the Democratic primary. Matthew Arndt (Green Party) and independents Elizabeth Fitzgibbon and Mike Thurow also qualified for the general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Glenn Grothman
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary with 99.7% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Wisconsin's 6th Congressional District (since 2015)

positions.summary: His official issues page says he supports repealing and replacing Obamacare with a more free-market system while keeping protections for pre-existing conditions.
positions.quote: I support repealing and replacing Obamacare with a more free-market system, while keeping parts of Obamacare that make sense, like protecting coverage for individuals with pre-existing conditions.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on the Budget, the Committee on Education and the Workforce, and the Committee on the Judiciary, and chairs the Health Care and Financial Services Subcommittee of the Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.researchNotes: No current statement of 2026 campaign priorities was found on his Ballotpedia profile or official site as of the research date.

candidates.name: Bradley Smith
candidates.ballotNote: Defeated Amanda Bell 50.3%-49.7% in the Democratic primary.

priorities.text: Says he will focus on rewarding companies that hire locally, fighting for livable wages, and making affordability a priority.
Says every Wisconsinite deserves affordable, dependable healthcare, and wants to build a low-cost public option to compete with private insurance.
priorities.quote: Healthcare should be a basic right in the richest country in the world.

priorities.text: Says he wants to increase public school funding and expand access to technical colleges and apprenticeships.

positions.summary: Candidate survey says he will work to lower healthcare costs, protect coverage for preexisting conditions, and build a low-cost public option available to all.
Campaign site says he supports universal background checks, red flag laws and secure storage.
positions.quote: I support common-sense safety measures such as universal background checks, red flag laws, and secure storage.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he will defend reproductive freedom.
positions.quote: We’ll defend reproductive freedom and ensure women, not politicians, have the right to make their own healthcare choices.

positions.summary: Campaign site says he will invest in solar and wind and aims for Wisconsin to lead in the clean energy transition.
positions.quote: That means investing in solar and wind, promoting clean water standards, and ensuring WI leads in clean energy transition.

candidates.researchNotes: Smith has not held elected office, so there is no official voting or legislative record. Ballotpedia lists Neenah as his birthplace while his campaign site says he was born in Larsen; the campaign account is used here.

candidates.name: Matthew Arndt

priorities.text: Names breaking up concentrated economic power (monopolies, Wall Street, private equity) as a central message.
priorities.quote: Break the grip of concentrated economic power.

priorities.text: Lists his "red lines" on his campaign site, including breaking up monopolies and Medicare for All.
Lists ending forever wars and stopping data centers among his positions.

positions.summary: Campaign site lists Medicare for All among his positions.
Campaign site says he supports a tax on large banks' profits to help pay down the national debt.
positions.quote: That is why I support a Wall Street mega-bank tax

record.text: Charged with misdemeanor disorderly conduct in connection with an Oct. 8, 2026 road rage incident in Mequon, Wisconsin. The other driver told investigators Arndt tailgated him; Arndt told WISN the other driver followed him into a gas station and harassed him, and denied the driver's account of his driving. A charge is not a finding of guilt; he is scheduled to appear in court on Nov. 3, 2026.

candidates.researchNotes: Positions and priorities come from his campaign site (endthecartel.com) and his 2026 Ballotpedia survey. His site's text on Israel concerns foreign aid and ties generally and was not recorded as a position on military aid. Arndt has a campaign website (End the Cartel) and completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; no independent news profile of his career or education was found, so the biography relies on his own materials.

statements.quote: That means reducing the risk of unnecessary wars and nuclear escalation, protecting Social Security and Medicare, confronting climate change, and taking seriously the economic and social consequences of rapidly expanding artificial intelligence and data centers.
statements.context: In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey (2026)

candidates.name: Elizabeth Fitzgibbon

priorities.text: Says affordability should be Congress's top priority and calls for reducing federal spending, opposing policies that raise everyday costs, and restoring fiscal responsibility.
Says government must be transparent, accountable, and limited, and criticizes both parties for allowing power to concentrate in unelected federal agencies.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from her Ballotpedia survey and campaign website. Her site's 12-priority 'Solutions' page is video-based; its text covers monetary policy and constitutional review, not the guide's issues. Fitzgibbon's family-law case is described only in her own campaign materials and Candidate Connection survey; it was not independently verified, and no occupation or employer is stated in the sources found.

statements.quote: Make housing more attainable by supporting practical solutions that expand supply, strengthen communities, and help working families stay rooted where they live.

candidates.name: Mike Thurow

priorities.text: Says he wants to break up monopolies he says price-gouge consumers and producers, and to make housing more affordable by expanding supply, easing development regulations, and barring investment firms from buying single-family homes and apartments.
Says that as a firefighter he wants more local input into public safety work and FEMA funding.
Says he would ban elected officials from trading stocks or cryptocurrency, push for term limits, and ban corporate PAC money in elections.

positions.summary: Candidate survey says he wants to make housing more affordable by expanding supply and cutting back on regulations limiting housing development.
positions.quote: Making housing more affordable by expanding the supply, cutting back on regulations limiting housing development, and banning investment firms from buying single family homes and apartments.

candidates.researchNotes: Statements come from his Ballotpedia survey and campaign platform page. His platform's first-responder funding, drug-pricing and defense-spending sections were not recorded as positions on the guide's issue statements. No further biographical details (birthplace, education, employer) appear in the sources found.

statements.quote: We can lower taxes for regular Americans without raising the deficit by closing corporate tax loopholes, targeting wasteful government spending, and cracking down on fraud.
